context_requirements: Expression of chloride channels/transporters (ANO1, ClC-3/CLCN3, ABCC1) or gap junctions (GJA1) that the drug can block
Intact apoptotic machinery (BAX/BAK, caspase-3) for the apoptosis-related arm
PI3K/AKT signaling active, since NPPB effects on proliferation/migration are PI3K/AKT-dependent
Proliferating cells for antiproliferative/arrest readouts; quiescent lines show little transcriptional change
falsifiers: No change in proliferation/arrest genes (CCND1, CDKN1A, E2F2) at 24 h in any of the nine lines
No induction of stress/apoptosis markers (DDIT4, TRIB3, GADD45A, PMAIP1) at either time point
Transcriptional response indistinguishable from vehicle across all lines (kinetics 'none')
Strong, uniform up-regulation of proliferation genes at 24 h, opposite to the predicted antiproliferative direction

evidence.supports: Chloride channel blocker DIDS reduces apoptosis-related proteins PARP-1 and AIF in neurons, indicating chloride channel blockade modulates apoptosis
Chloride channel blocker NPPB prevents emodin-induced apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells, linking chloride channels to proliferation/apoptosis control
NPPB induces apoptosis of human lens epithelial cells via ROS and ER stress through the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway
NPPB modulates apoptosis, proliferation, migration and ECM synthesis of conjunctival fibroblasts by inhibiting PI3K/AKT signaling
Chloride channel blocker abolishes hyperglycemia-induced ClC-3-associated hippocampal neuronal apoptosis
